page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.2xlarge is an instance belonging to the High Clock Speed family, powered by a KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 6149 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 8 vCPUs distributed across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 22 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set features include AVX-512F, AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, while local storage is not bundled and network throughput provides a 2 Gbps baseline. No discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In benchmark evaluations, multi-threaded CPU performance achieves average results, with a PassMark CPU score of 8280.79 and stress-ng multi-core processing at 7203.49. Instruction-level tests also show steady mid-tier capability, reflected in PassMark extended instructions reaching 6463.65 and Clang software compilation at 6770.0. However, single-core execution is lower relative to modern platforms, registering 1091.0 on Geekbench and 1355.68 on stress-ng. Memory subsystems display a notable contrast: small-block cached read bandwidth reaches 402.4 GB/sec, while uncached 256 MB reads settle at 38.98 GB/sec, resulting in a weak PassMark memory score of 1558.95.

From a workload perspective, the instance is equipped for tasks requiring dedicated x86 compute with modest RAM footprints, such as build compilation, continuous integration pipelines, batch processing, and caching layers with Redis SET performance reaching 7.08 million operations per second. Tradeoffs center on the absence of included local disks, modest 2 Gbps networking, weak single-thread performance, and limited throughput on medium-sized language models and database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.2xlarge is a compute-oriented instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6149 processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores alongside 16.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX-512F, AVX, and AES. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPUs, and networking is limited to a 2 Gbps baseline. Benchmarks indicate balanced mid-tier multi-core compute capability, demonstrated by an 8280.79 PassMark CPU score, Clang software compilation of 6770.0, and 7.08 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core compute and uncached memory bandwidth show comparatively weak efficiency. This configuration fits continuous integration agents, general batch compute, build servers, and mid-tier in-memory caching where high per-thread burst speeds or dense memory allocations are not mandatory.
